# Power Manager Fast FSM Behavioral Specification

## Overview

This module implements the fast-clock-domain power management sequencer. It is responsible for moving the system between the following major operating conditions:

- Power-on / power-up sequencing
- Normal active operation
- Low-power entry, low-power exit, low-power fall-through, and low-power abort
- Reset handling

The module shall start from a fully reset, low-power condition and, upon request, bring the system through clock enablement, reset release, OTP initialization, life-cycle initialization, ROM integrity checking, and into active operation. After active operation is reached, the module shall respond to low-power entry requests and reset requests.

## Reset Behavior

When the module’s reset is asserted, it shall:

- Enter its low-power resting state.
- Keep all clock enable requests deasserted.
- Assert all life-cycle and system reset requests for all power domains.
- Deassert the power-up acknowledgement and the power-down request.
- Record the reset cause as “undefined”.
- Assert the low-power indication.
- Keep the processing-element fetch enable deasserted.

The module shall remain in this state until it receives a power-up request or has an internally pending reset-completion condition to process.

## Power-Up Sequence

When the module is in its low-power resting state and receives a power-up request, it shall begin the power-up sequence.

### Clock Enablement

The module shall request that the main and I/O clock domains be enabled. It shall remain in the clock-enable step until the clock status indicates that all requested clocks are enabled.

The USB clock request shall be asserted only if USB clocking is permitted by the USB enable input. The module shall also provide a USB clock status output that reflects the status of the USB clock.

### Reset Release

After clocks are enabled, the module shall deassert the reset requests for all life-cycle and system reset domains. It shall wait until the reset status indicates that the life-cycle reset domains are released before continuing.

### OTP Initialization

The module shall assert the OTP initialization request and wait for the OTP completion indication before proceeding.

### Life-Cycle Initialization

The module shall assert the life-cycle controller initialization request and wait for the life-cycle completion indication before proceeding.

### Power-Up Acknowledgement

After OTP and life-cycle initialization complete, the module shall assert the power-up acknowledgement unless the current power-up sequence is part of completing an internal reset cycle.

The module shall keep the acknowledgement asserted until the power-up request is withdrawn, or until the module determines that the power-up sequence is actually part of an internal reset cycle.

When leaving this step, the module shall:

- Deassert the power-up acknowledgement.
- Clear the configuration lock.
- Assert a wake-up indication if the power-up was caused by a wakeup event and the previous reset cause was low-power entry.
- Clear the internal reset-completion state.

### Strap Sampling

The module shall initiate strap sampling during every cold-boot / reset power-up sequence. The strap output shall be asserted for this purpose only if the strap has not already been sampled since the last time all system reset domains were asserted.

Once relevant, the module shall proceed to the ROM integrity check step.

### ROM Integrity Check

The module shall clear the low-power indication and clear the recorded reset cause to “none” when the ROM check step begins.

The module shall wait for the ROM integrity check to indicate that the ROM check is done. If the ROM check is disabled, the “done” condition shall be treated as true.

After the ROM check is done, the module shall wait for the ROM integrity check to indicate that the ROM is good. If the ROM check is disabled, the “good” condition shall be treated as true.

The ROM integrity check shall be treated as disabled when the life-cycle controller indicates that both DFT enable and hardware debug enable are active. In that case, the module shall not require a good ROM check result.

When both ROM check conditions are satisfied, the module shall enter the active state.

## Active State

In the active state, the module shall:

- Assert the processing-element fetch enable.
- Remain in active operation until a reset request or a low-power entry request is received.

When a reset request or low-power entry request is received, the module shall:

- Deassert the processing-element fetch enable.
- Clear the recorded reset cause to “undefined”.
- Begin disabling the clocks.

## Clock Disable and Path Selection

The module shall request that the main and I/O clocks be disabled. It shall wait until the clock status indicates that the clocks are disabled.

Once the clocks are disabled:

- If a reset request is pending, the module shall enter the reset path.
- If no reset request is pending, the module shall enter the low-power path and assert the low-power indication.

If the clocks do not become disabled and a direct reset request is pending, the module shall not wait for clock-disable completion and shall immediately enter the reset path. Direct reset requests are those caused by escalation or by an unstable main power indication.

## Low-Power Path

### Fall-Through Handling

After the clocks are disabled, if the low-power entry request is no longer asserted, the module shall treat the entry as a fall-through.

In this case, the module shall:

- Clear the low-power hint.
- Re-enable the clocks.
- Assert the fall-through indication.
- Assert the wake-up indication.
- Return to the ROM check sequence, and from there back to active state.

### Non-Volatile Idle Check

If the low-power entry request is still asserted, the module shall check whether the OTP controller, life-cycle controller, and flash controller are idle.

If any of those controllers is busy, the module shall abort the low-power entry. In this case, the module shall:

- Re-enable the clocks.
- Assert the abort indication.
- Assert the wake-up indication.
- Return to the ROM check sequence, and from there back to active state.

### Low-Power Preparation

If all non-volatile controllers are idle, the module shall proceed with low-power entry.

The module shall record the reset cause as “low-power entry”.

The module shall then make the appropriate reset decisions based on whether the main power domain remains powered:

- If the main power domain is being powered down, the module shall assert life-cycle and system reset requests for all non-always-on power domains.
- If the main power domain remains powered, the non-always-on reset requests shall not be asserted for this purpose.

The module shall wait until the reset status is consistent with the low-power entry condition. This is satisfied when either the main power domain remains on, or all non-always-on reset domains have been asserted.

### Power-Down Request

After the reset status is consistent, the module shall:

- Assert the power-down request.
- Wait for the power-down acknowledgement.
- Deassert the power-down request.
- Enter the low-power resting state.

In the low-power resting state, the module shall wait for a power-up request. The power-up request may be caused by a wakeup event or by a reset event.

## Reset Path

The reset path is entered when a reset request is pending after the clock-disable step, or when a direct reset request occurs while clocks are still being disabled.

When the reset path is entered, the module shall:

- Clear the low-power hint.
- Mark the power-up sequence as an internal reset-completion sequence.

### Reset Preparation

The module shall record the reset cause as “hardware request”.

The module shall assert all life-cycle reset requests for all power domains.

The module shall assert system reset requests for all power domains in response to:

- Peripheral reset requests.
- Direct reset requests.
- Software reset requests.

For a non-debug-module reset request, the module shall assert the system reset requests only when the life-cycle hardware debug enable is not active. If hardware debug enable is active, the non-debug-module reset request shall not assert the system reset domains.

### Reset Wait

The module shall wait until the reset status confirms that all requested reset domains are asserted.

If the reset was triggered by a main-power unstable reset request, the module shall assert a clear request for that main-power reset request and shall remain in the reset wait state until that request is withdrawn.

When the reset wait condition is satisfied, the module shall return to the low-power resting state with the reset-completion state set. This causes the module to automatically begin the power-up sequence without requiring a new power-up request.

## Reset versus Low-Power Priority

If a reset request and a low-power entry request are both pending when the clock-disable step completes, the module shall select the reset path.

Once the module has committed to either the reset path or the low-power path, it shall not re-evaluate the other pending request until it reaches the next resting state. Pending requests are handled on a first-committed basis.

## Invalid State Handling

If the module receives an invalid-state indication, it shall immediately enter its terminal invalid state.

In this terminal state, the module shall:

- Assert all life-cycle reset requests.
- Assert all system reset requests.
- Disable all clock enable requests.
- Remain in this state until reset.

The module shall not attempt to recover from this state on its own.

## Summary of Output Behavior

- The module shall provide power-up acknowledgement and power-down request outputs as part of the low-power coordination.
- The module shall provide separate life-cycle and system reset request outputs, together with a reset cause output for the reset manager.
- The module shall request main, I/O, and USB clock enables as appropriate.
- The module shall provide wake-up, fall-through, abort, clear-hint, and clear-configuration-lock indications.
- The module shall provide OTP and life-cycle initialization requests.
- The module shall provide a strap sampling output.
- The module shall provide a low-power status indication.
- The module shall provide a processing-element fetch enable that is asserted only in the active state.
- The module shall provide a clear request for a main-power unstable reset condition while waiting for that reset request to be withdrawn.
